items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: Of course, our act, Modern Cocktail -- that was their second time around so they had a reputation in vaudeville.

ctx.x: No, he hadn't trained or anything. No, he was dancing everyday, that's the only thing. Doing his knee drops and -- so the boy said -- George said, "Don't hit me hard because I just finished eating because I didn't think I was going to fight." Then in Spanish, they had an interpreter, "I won't hit you hard." George went in there and boxed around, careless, and the boy hit George and knocked George down. Instead of George falling, he did a flip back -- he was a tumbler, too, you know. He did a back flip and come up…
Mr. Bushell, can you think of any more memorable incidents?

items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: a little guy named George State, and he was a feather weight... So George said, 'I'll fight him.'

ctx.x: Yeah, professional, yeah. And I think Paulino -- I saw Paulino there, Paulino Scodoon. He was on one of the cards. Anyhow, one of the boxers didn't show up, so they said, 'We're one bout short.' So we had a Russian dancer, a little guy named George State, and he was a feather weight. He had done some pro boxing but he wasn't good enough, so he went back to doing dancing, Russian dancing -- knee drops and all that sort of thing. So, they said, 'We're short a bout.' So George said, 'I'll fight him.' 'Come on,…

was a middle weight and a heavy weight bout. This feather weight champion was supposed to box an exhibition bout with somebody and the guy didn't show up, I guess he got cold feet. George said, "I'll fight him."
